A-keep.response: All hostile labels remain supported obligations: exact bytes from one coherent snapshot, host-state restoration and whole retained decisions must survive each recorded ambient hop. Known cost/classification holds remain; no finite poison pass proves every caller safe.

A-coop.response: The proposed amendment excludes hostile ambient mutation, not ordinary __proto__, immutable snapshots, accidental accessors/cycles or atomic decisions. Keep meter, explicit settlement and whole fault oracles; retain each excluded hostile witness with its narrowed claim, never call it repaired.

A-bytes.response: Move ordinary snapshot and meter cases to the cooperative wrapper, preserve core byte/field identity and full decision oracles. Hostile ambient witnesses become scoped limitations only after amendment; bytes in one mutable realm do not make them harmless.

A-hard.response: Use every hostile label in hardening-corpus.json, eight binding hops, prototype comparison and current frozen positive failures. Require durable pinning plus compatibility. Proxy disagreement/getter execution and static inventory gaps stay obligations; never infer whole-decision integrity from a failed poison installation.

B-keep.response: Replay own-index and descriptor-conversion channels, iterator next/result and global replacement with the current save/restore discipline; retain depth/list/diagnostic cost cases and failed-environment refusals. Source audit plus these cases must explain which ambient reads are covered.

B-coop.response: Differentially preserve ordinary bytes, __proto__, diagnostics and old-view immutability while charging traversal/list/stack work. Hostile prototype/global witnesses remain recorded exclusions after the proposed stable-realm amendment, not a claimed serializer fix.

B-bytes.response: Wrapper retains ordinary coherence, canonical vectors, metering and diagnostics; strict core/adapter have independent byte spelling, duplication and scan/allocation cases. Preserve whole state/replay behavior; do not use wrapper poison or N15 results as parser evidence.

B-hard.response: Check the exact dependency read graph against binding and two-hop iterator witnesses; all binding replacements must be ineffectual. Current Kernel frozen refusal rejects a support claim. Descriptor/read disagreement, getters and the traversal meter are not discharged by freezing.

C-hold.response: Every domain/exotic witness stays a known defect or corrected historical domain case, linked to the responsible amendment and root consumers. Proxy hidden-target replay is reproduced, not assigned an answer. This option closes triage only.

C-brand.response: Keep canonical/transport domain distinctions and ordinary Unicode/number/__proto__ vectors. Non-Proxy unsupported brands refuse before listing in all root consumers. Forwarding Proxies follow one of the two explicit unchosen PROXY-01 outcomes; slot checks alone cannot promise refusal.

C-project.response: Projection needs its own amended logical-domain and equality rule for bare and forwarded targets; run same/different hidden contents and ordinary canonical vectors through every root. Current refusal contract and owner direction reject adoption here.

C-bytes.response: Core refuses live object inputs and strictly validates canonical values; wrapper preserves ordinary domain and refuses unsupported non-Proxy brands before listing. Its Proxy policy still needs the named owner answer; adapter rejects decoded duplicates before erasure.

D1.response: Re-audit each current authority, identity, delivery/history and commit path against the recorded cases; full return/view/grant/history/next receipt must agree. Source inventory edits alone cannot prove missed read syntax or early mutation absent.

D2.response: Private constructors/planners/immutable plans and one state writer must block the recorded authority/identity/history/early-write bypasses. Preserve every whole-decision observation and delivery boundary. Core-independent; sequencing after binding does not discharge a case.

E1.response: Each existing parser, oracle, sweep and mutant runner must reproduce its own declared cases, with controls and explicit surviving mutants/coverage gaps. Presence in a catalog cannot certify source reach or a complete comparison.

E2.response: TOOLS-01 maps every inventoried artifact to a maintained case or reasoned retirement; missing cases, comparison omissions and N15 survival remain failures of the corresponding gate. The one registry preserves provenance; it is not itself a semantic oracle.

E3.response: Module/ownership escape tests supplement mapped runtime scenarios; they cannot replace the parser grammar, full comparisons or early-write observations. Retire analyzer artifacts only after each obligation has structural or retained runtime evidence.

F1.response: Recompute record facts for each candidate and manually inspect authority/status meaning, including held and accepted-but-unintegrated histories. A valid link or hash cannot replace accessible evidence.

F2.response: Generate SHA/count/interval/allowlist facts and deliberately corrupt each field; preserve human authority provenance and held-status semantics. Automation does not manufacture adoption or settle a prose ambiguity.

F01K.response: Every recorded lifecycle counterexample is a relation-table row with both orders and legal terminal result; unimplemented K1.3 behavior is a future gate, not an omitted case.

F01R.response: Map those same relations to model edges and distinguish cancellation/completion and generation/deadline mutants. Reject unmapped relations and conflicting accepted effects; no new lifecycle semantics are chosen.

F02K.response: Canonical-domain and codec cases remain required alongside the interim brand matrix. Add all forwarding-Proxy witnesses; acceptance narrows the restored non-Proxy claim, refusal needs an amendment. Root-level forbidden state/receipt effects are checked under either answer.

F02R.response: Port ordinary canonical-domain, UTF-8/duplicate and equality cases to strict core plus wrapper/adapter. Hidden non-Proxy state must not silently project; forwarding-Proxy policy remains conditional and interim acceptance precedes relocation.

F03K.response: Use actual producer-to-validator paths at identity limits plus revoked-Proxy invalid-text refusal; alternate hidden/visible executions to expose shared counters and preserve all refusal effects.

F03R.response: Private constructors prevent cross-scope collision and raw sequence access; bypass tests plus the same maximum-length downstream round trips and total malformed diagnostics distinguish the refactor from types alone.

F04K.response: Check every disposition against reachable entry points and consumers at pinned H; external unknowns stay explicit and a historical retirement claim is not current reachability evidence.

F04R.response: Generate the same reachability facts and reject a new forbidden edge or stale disposition. Human-authored migration obligations still determine what may retire; graphs cannot infer external consumers.

F05K.response: For each recorded oracle failure, vary its missing material field and legal schedule, including no external call; inspect the entire decision and next receipt, not only an assertion count.

F05R.response: One complete-result schema must include each missing state/effect/receipt dimension with independent legal relations and omission mutants. A shared partial schema would reproduce the family defect.

F06K.response: Run every grammar/normalization/relation counterexample through the maintained parser, asserting whole rows and exact equality. Retain enclosing-context and Unicode cases, not merely happy-path tables.

F06R.response: Move the governing relation to structured data and distinguish duplicate/unknown rows and stale renders. Keep dependency scanner syntax/escape cases separately; a renderer does not prove the dependency analysis.

F07K.response: Verify all recorded identity/evidence/authority mistakes against immutable commits and accessible artifacts; explicitly distinguish review, acceptance, integration and release.

F07R.response: Generate objective facts and corrupt each field to check rejection; owner quotations and independent verdicts remain sourced human records. Inaccessible raw payload remains a failure even with a digest.

F08K.response: Bound the current-sentence search and compare each domain/ownership/status claim to its canonical owner, including durability and held states. Historical prose is evidence, not authority.

F08R.response: Route current claims to canonical owners without erasing historical evidence; challenge every enumerated consumer with a stale/stronger claim. Navigation checks do not close semantic consistency.

F09K.response: Include all hostile labels, global Object replacement in getPrototypeOf and both iterator hops, own __proto__, unsupported-error/refusal and recovery-history channels. Full canonical/state observations and correct environmental refusal are required; flags alone do not protect globals.

F09R.response: Amend hostile ambient guarantees explicitly, then preserve ordinary snapshot/__proto__/fault cases in wrapper and core. Retain excluded hostile witnesses as limits; fixed history/host ownership and explicit settlement remain useful even under cooperation.

F10K.response: Derive charged abstract operations over every depth/alias/string/diagnostic shape; preserve independent roots and exact weights. Sealed timing observations motivate the meter but are not rerun or used as gates; N15 still needs a distinguishing kill.

F10R.response: Carry the same object-work and diagnostic counterexamples into the wrapper, including N15; derive separate scan/allocation bounds for core and adapter with exact cap edges and no aggregate semantic cap. Byte length alone is insufficient.

F11K.response: Enumerate recorded authority and callback orders, compare whole decisions and next positions, and ensure a replay/content check cannot disclose or overrule missing authority.

F11R.response: Planner/apply boundary and current-version precondition must reject raw/forged plans and stale-after-callback commits; replay the same full precedence table under the preserved authority contract.

F12K.response: Each retained-history counterexample needs required writer/epoch/absence facts and immutable old views across all transition routes, including refusals and retries.

F12R.response: Required tagged history in every plan plus own optional records and read-only projections must reject omitted-history/writable-view bypasses. Keep the original alternate-transition observations as evidence.

F13K.response: Explicit settlement avoids observing returned Promise species; exercise late/duplicate delivery, single bound read and writer attribution with unchanged intent/receipt/acknowledgment state.

F13R.response: Transport must preserve those local delivery decisions while adding peer/capability/replay checks. Remote authentication is additional evidence; bytes neither require remote transport nor prove its correctness.

F14K.response: Reapply each mutant at its exact site with a passing control and causal test failure; distinguish a timeout, harness error or surviving N15 from a kill.

F14R.response: Registry enforces source/control/oracle identities and mappings for the same cases; a semantic survivor remains open until a meaningful new oracle rejects it. No registry-count substitute for a kill.

F15K.response: Quoted/computed/assignment destructuring and partial/nested predicates remain explicit guard gaps; runtime poison and full early-write/next-receipt observations close only their declared schedules.

F15R.response: Null-prototype optional data removes inherited reads; sole state ownership prevents early writes only if every bypass is excluded. Preserve observed decisions and map all retired analyzer obligations to checks, without a future-TypeScript soundness claim.

F16K.response: Enumerate every reached exit and each whole-result comparison, including no-call outcomes and next receipts; missing operations/fields remain gaps despite green sweeps.

F16R.response: Registry separates scenarios, adapters and independently derived complete legal outcomes; omission and wrong-comparison mutants must fail. Only hostile-profile gates retire on accepted binding migration, never fault/state observations.
